content:
Subtraction with borrowing is where many Class 2 children lose Olympiad marks. This guide sets out what the IMO Class 2 subtraction chapter tests, the facts that fix most errors, and a free 10-question test with answers.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Subtraction chapter tests

  • 2-digit and 3-digit subtraction, with and without borrowing
  • Missing-number sentences like ▢ − 20 = 60
  • Checking a subtraction by adding back
  • Word problems using "left", "fewer" and "how many more"

Key facts your child should know

  • Subtract the ones first, then tens, then hundreds; borrow when the top digit is too small.
  • Borrowing takes 1 from the next column and adds 10 to the current one.
  • Check by adding back: if 90 − 35 = 55, then 55 + 35 = 90.
  • "How many more" means subtract the smaller from the larger.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Subtracting the smaller ones digit from the larger regardless of position.
  • Forgetting to reduce the next column after borrowing.
  • Reading "how many more" as an addition.

quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Borrow across the zero: a 0 becomes 9 after lending. So 800 − 529 = 271.

questions.q: Subtract 98 from 615 in your head. What is the answer?
questions.explanation: Take away 100 first: 615 − 100 = 515. You took 2 too many, so give back 2: 515 + 2 = 517.
The ones need a borrow: take 1 ten from 84. Then 84 − 29 = 55.
Borrow across the zero: a 0 becomes 9 after lending. So 703 − 458 = 245.

questions.q: Subtract 99 from 840 in your head. What is the answer?
questions.explanation: Take away 100 first: 840 − 100 = 740. You took 1 too many, so give back 1: 740 + 1 = 741.
No borrowing is needed. Subtract ones, tens and hundreds: 654 − 321 = 333.
Only the hundreds change: 9 hundreds − 4 hundreds. So 945 − 400 = 545.

questions.q: A dairy sent 250 milk bottles to a shop. 86 bottles were sold by noon. How many bottles are unsold?

questions.explanation: No borrowing is needed. Subtract ones, tens and hundreds: 795 − 342 = 453.

faq.a: When the top digit is smaller than the bottom one, you take one from the next column, turning it into 10 extra so you can subtract.

faq.q: How can a child check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add the answer to the number taken away. If it gives back the starting number, the answer is right.
